title: Parkinsonism Co-occurrence Among Older Autistic Adults, Adults With Intellectual Disability, and a Control Sample of Adults in National Health Care Claims Data.
abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that Parkinson's Disease (PD)-related conditions (i.e., parkinsonism) co-occur more commonly with autism than in the general population. However, prior prevalence-based studies did not account for the influence of antipsychotic usage, which is linked to secondary parkinsonism as a possible side effect, or co-occurring intellectual disability (ID). In addition, no study of incidence rates of parkinsonism among older autistic adults has been completed to date. Prevalence and incidence were examined among 56,970,786 45+ year old persons across four groups (autism only, ID only, autism + ID, and control sample) utilizing U.S.-based, individually linked Medicaid and Medicare health care claims data from 2017 to 2019. Compared with the control sample (1.57%), highly elevated prevalence of co-occurring PD-related diagnoses was found across groups (autism only: 3.83%; ID only: 4.32%; autism + ID: 4.86%). This elevation in prevalence persisted after the exclusion of individuals prescribed antipsychotic medications. Whether examining broader or narrower (excluding secondary) parkinsonism, the age-standardized incidence or risk of newly documented co-occurring parkinsonism was highest in those with autism + ID, followed by those with autism only and those with ID only, all of which far outpaced control sample findings. title: Photobiomodulation in Parkinson's disease: From pathogenesis to intervention.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder clinically characterized by bradykinesia, rest tremor, rigidity, and postural instability. Its core pathological features include the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons within the substantia nigra pars compacta, striatal dopamine depletion, and intracellular accumulation of misfolded α-Synuclein (α-Syn)-rich Lewy inclusions that trigger neuronal dysfunction and cell death. Despite substantial research efforts, existing pharmacological strategies targeting α-Syn and dopaminergic neurons show limited capacity to halt or reverse PD progression, creating an urgent need for novel alternative therapeutic interventions. Photobiomodulation (PBM) is a non-invasive phototherapy that delivers photonic energy to biological tissues using visible and near-infrared light. Preclinical studies have documented neuroprotective signals linked to PBM in experimental PD models; however, clinical studies to date provide only preliminary and inconsistent evidence regarding safety and possible symptomatic benefit. This narrative review outlines the mechanistic rationale, preclinical findings, clinical observations, and key translational limitations for PBM as an investigational adjunctive intervention in PD. We first elaborate on PD-related pathological mechanisms, followed by an in-depth discussion of PBM-mediated biological actions, and consolidate recent evidence for its anti-PD applications in preclinical settings. Available preclinical data suggest PBM could modulate mitochondrial function, neuroinflammation, dopaminergic-neuron survival, and responses along the microbiota-gut-brain axis in experimental PD models, though direct evidence supporting modification of α-synuclein aggregation or propagation remains sparse. Clinical observations support procedural feasibility and acceptable short-term safety profiles. Nevertheless, definitive clinical efficacy cannot be confirmed given small sample sizes, heterogeneous intervention protocols, and inconsistent outcomes from controlled trials. PBM should currently be regarded as an investigational adjunctive strategy rather than an established therapy for PD.

title: Comprehension of ambiguous sentences in Alzheimer's disease: A study with Brazilian older adults.
abstract:
Language impairment is an early marker in Alzheimer's disease (AD), manifesting in both semantic memory and syntactic comprehension. The comprehension of lexical (LAS) and syntactic (SAS) ambiguous sentences requires the integrity of both systems and is particularly challenging for patients with probable AD. The study aimed to investigate differences in performance on ambiguous sentence comprehension between healthy older adults and patients with probable AD, and to identify which type of ambiguity posed the greatest difficulty for each group.
A cross-sectional observational study with 118 participants (60 patients with probable AD and 58 healthy controls) underwent an experimental task of comprehending 12 ambiguous sentences (6 LAS and 6 SAS). Multiple linear regression models were adjusted for age, sex, and education.
Patients with probable AD performed significantly worse in LAS (β = -4.664; 95% CI: -5.827 to -3.502; p < 0.001), SAS (β = -3.259; 95% CI: -4.294 to -2.225; p < 0.001), and TAS (β = -7.776; 95% CI: -9.624 to -5.927; p < 0.001). Both groups interpreted LAS significantly better than SAS. Education was associated with better performance in all three models (p < 0.05). Age and sex were not significantly associated.
Patients with probable AD present significantly impaired comprehension of ambiguous sentences, with syntactic ambiguity posing the greatest challenge. Education proved to be a protective factor. These findings reinforce the multifactorial nature of linguistic deficits in probable AD and suggest that the ambiguous sentences task is a useful tool for assessing linguistic impairment.

title: Geissoschizine methyl ether can be simultaneously measured with rhynchophylline and hirsutine in Yokukansan extract.
abstract: Yokukansan (YKS) is a Kampo prescription used to treat neurosis, insomnia, and behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD). Previous studies have reported that geissoschizine methyl ether (GM), an indole alkaloid from Uncaria species, is the principal active constituent of YKS in the treatment of BPSD. Within YKS, GM originates from Uncaria Hook (UH), a component of natural drugs. Rhynchophylline (RIN) and hirsutine (HIR) are specified as quantitative marker constituents of YKS in the Japanese Pharmacopoeia 18th Revision (JP18) to determine the total alkaloid content. Given the recent focus on the pharmacological activity of GM, this study examined an HPLC method for detecting GM, RIN, and HIR in YKS extracts. RIN, HIR, and GM were detected as well-resolved peaks in the YKS extract under JP18 assay conditions. Comparison with the Uncaria Hook-depleted YKS extract showed no apparent matrix interference at the retention times of these alkaloids. In addition, this method was applied to most of the tested C18 columns, meeting the JP18 specifications. These findings indicate that the Japanese Pharmacopoeia assay framework can be extended to enable concurrent measurement of GM, RIN, and HIR in YKS extracts, thereby providing additional alkaloid information without requiring a separate GM-specific assay.

title: Emerging links between gut dysbiosis, aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation, and Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder, is classically defined as a motor disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra and motor dysfunction. Increasing evidence, however, identifies PD as a multisystem disorder with early non-motor features, including sleep, psychiatric, and gastrointestinal disturbances, implicating the gut-brain axis. Tryptophan metabolism through serotonin, kynurenine, and indole pathways generates bioactive metabolites, many of which regulate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). AhR is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic metabolism through canonical signaling pathways; however, growing evidence supports its role in immune balance, glial responses, and barrier integrity. Altered AhR signaling may therefore connect gut dysbiosis and disrupted tryptophan metabolism to sustained, systemic and central inflammation in PD. This review examines gut dysbiosis, tryptophan metabolism, and AhR signaling as potential mechanisms underlying idiopathic PD and highlights their relevance to early diagnosis and disease-modifying therapies.

title: Teamwork in Parkinson's care: Building multidisciplinary models worldwide.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a complex, progressive neurodegenerative disorder requiring comprehensive, long-term management. PD affects millions of people globally and presents with motor and non-motor symptoms that progressively impair function and quality of life. While pharmacological therapy remains effective, optimal care extends beyond medication management. Traditional care models for PD often rely heavily on doctors and primarily target motor symptoms and motor complications, with less attention to non-motor symptoms, many of which remain under-recognized. This imbalance contributes to fragmented care and unmet patient needs. These challenges highlight the need for a multidisciplinary care team to address the full spectrum of patient needs. Therefore, integrating a multidisciplinary approach is essential for comprehensive PD management. This manuscript proposes a scalable, multidisciplinary care team model designed to optimise clinical outcomes, enhance quality of life, and remain adaptable across diverse healthcare systems worldwide. It addresses global challenges associated with MDT implementation and outlines potential future solutions. The manuscript also highlights stakeholder engagement in Community Engagement and Involvement (CEI), including initiatives in Tanzania and Thailand to raise community awareness. In particular, the "CheckPD" project and integrated "eat, move, sleep" lifestyle interventions promote lifestyle-based strategies for PD prevention and improved long-term management of PD. Overall, the model emphasises coordinated, patient-centred care that integrates medical, rehabilitative, psychological, and social support services.

title: A First Case of Compulsive Amnestic Sleep-Related Shopping Induced by Pramipexole Therapy of Restless Legs Syndrome.
abstract: Dopamine receptor agonists (DAs) such as pramipexole/ropinirole are recognized treatments for restless legs syndrome (RLS) and Parkinson's disease (PD). It is well established that these medications can cause impulse control disorders (ICDs) during wakefulness, side effects with serious and potentially life-altering consequences. Impulse control disorders are recurrent difficult-to-resist behaviors that can be harmful to the patient or others around them. Common examples include pathologic gambling and compulsive sexual behaviors, eating, and shopping. We present the case of a patient with RLS who developed pathologic nocturnal sleep-related shopping, without recalling the events, which resolved after discontinuing pramipexole. This case illustrates the devastating consequences that unrecognized medically-induced ICDs can have on patients' lives and the importance of counseling patients about ICDs during wake and sleep prior to starting DA therapy.

title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and alterations in kynurenine pathway of tryptophan metabolism are associated with depression in people with HIV.
abstract:
People with HIV have increased risk of depression and differed gut microbiome composition. While alterations in gut microbiome and kynurenine pathway of tryptophan metabolism have each been independently linked to depression in the general population, their interrelationships in people with HIV remain unclear.
People with HIV with available gut microbiome data and depression assessments were included (n=365). We assessed the associations between gut microbiome, evidence of depression, kynurenine metabolites, inflammatory markers, clinical variables.
Individuals with evidence of depression (n=32) had significantly higher plasma levels of IL-6 and quinolinic acid, along with an altered gut microbiome composition (dysbiosis), compared to individuals without evidence of depression (n=333). No statistically significant correlation was found between depression-related gut microbial dysbiosis and kynurenine metabolites levels or inflammatory markers, whereas the latter two correlated with each other. Mediation analysis further showed a borderline but not statistically significant indirect effect of kynurenine and quinolinic acid levels on depression through inflammation.
Our data show that gut microbiome dysbiosis is associated with depression in people with HIV, but not with the altered kynurenine metabolites linked to depression. These findings suggest distinct pathways linking gut microbiome dysbiosis and alterations in kynurenine pathway of tryptophan metabolism to depression.

title: Chemsex as a temporal strategy: rethinking rush use in sexual behavior among Chinese urban MSM.
abstract:
This study examined how Chinese urban men who have sex with men use rush in sexual contexts to organize sexual encounters. Existing Chinese research has mainly discussed rush use in relation to HIV-related vulnerability, condomless sex and multiple partners. Less is known about how participants themselves understand its role in intimacy and everyday life. This study addresses that gap by analyzing rush use as a temporal strategy.
The study drew on life-story interviews with 24 men who have sex with men in four major Chinese cities. Participants had used rush in a sexual context within the previous 12 months. Interviews explored experiences of rush use, sexual settings, partner contexts, work schedules, family expectations and digital sexual practices. Data were analyzed through narrative reading and thematic coding, with attention to timing, sequence, duration, rhythm and return.
Participants described rush as more than a way to intensify sexual pleasure. They used it to reorganize sexual time through five practices: accelerating sexual initiation, prolonging encounters, creating temporary 'bubbles' away from work and family pressure, synchronizing bodily rhythms in group sex, and deferring responsibilities linked to marriage, disclosure and the future. These practices enabled fragile moments of intimacy, but also produced vulnerabilities, including compressed safety negotiation, fatigue, anxiety, exclusion, guilt and the return of everyday obligations.
Rush use among Chinese urban men who have sex with men should be understood not only through pleasure or risk, but also through its role in reshaping the temporal organization of intimacy. The study extends sexualized substance use research and queer temporality scholarship by showing how timing, pace, duration, and return shape risk, consent, care and aftercare. Sexual health and harm reduction approaches should therefore consider the temporal pressures under which sexual decisions are made.

title: Pilot study of a ChatGPT-based educational and counselling tool in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic.
abstract:
Real-world implementation of large language models such as ChatGPT to enhance patient education remains limited. We evaluated the feasibility, acceptability and attitudes towards a ChatGPT-based counselling tool among patients and healthcare workers (HCWs) in a specialist infectious diseases clinic.
We conducted a prospective clinical implementation study in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic in Singapore from Jan 2025 to December 2025. Patients interacted with a custom ChatGPT-based chatbot prior to routine counselling by physicians or pharmacists. Responses were reviewed with patients subsequently during consultation. Post-interaction, patients and HCWs completed structured surveys incorporating domains from a validated survey tool: perceived risk, anxiety, technology/social influence and intention for future use.
The chatbot was most frequently used for counselling on antiretroviral therapy initiation or switching, and sexual health advice. A total of 35 patients and 35 HCW assessments were analysed. Patients had greater perceived risk with the use of the chatbot compared to HCWs, as indicated by lower median scores (13, IQR 10-16; vs. 18, IQR 15-21), while anxiety scores were similar. Technology/social influence scores were high across both groups (overall median 20, IQR 19-22). Most participants indicated willingness for future use. Qualitative feedback highlighted improved patient understanding and more focused consultations, but concerns included lack of contextual nuance and occasional inaccuracies.
The pilot implementation of a ChatGPT-based counselling tool in a specialist HIV and sexual health clinic was feasible and generally acceptable to patients and HCWs. Further studies are required to evaluate accuracy and clinical effectiveness before broader implementation.

title: Prenatal Maternal Phosphatidylcholine and Children's Behavior and Cognition through 4 Years of Age: Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
Increasing popularity of choline supplements may prompt patients to seek advice on safe, effective doses during prenatal visits. Rationale for prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements stems from the fetal developmental role of α7-nicotinic cholinergic receptor gene CHRNA7, associated with Schizophrenia, Attention Deficit Disorder, and Autism Spectrum Disorder. Fetal brain developmental problems, including those linked to CHRNA7, convey risk for these mental illnesses. Choline derived from maternal phosphatidylcholine intake activates fetal α7-nicotinic receptors, which facilitate brain neurosynaptic development, observed after birth as robust inhibition of cerebral neurophysiological responses to repeated stimuli. A previous study found that maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo significantly improved newborns' neurophysiology and thereby decreased the children's attention and social withdrawal problems at 40 months of age.
To assess whether maternal prenatal phosphatidylcholine compared to placebo in a larger randomized clinical trial supports fetal brain development to decrease childhood attention and social behavioral problems and increase cognitive performance.
A clinical trial at University of Colorado Hospital Prenatal Clinics and affiliated community hospitals randomized 206 women to 9000 mg phosphatidylcholine (the form of choline occurring naturally in food) or placebo from 16 weeks' gestation through delivery. From 18 months to 4 years of age, 142 children were assessed by parents on the Child Behavior Check List 1.5-5-year version (CBCL1.5-5yr). The 2 primary outcomes were Withdrawn and Attention Problems. A secondary outcome was the Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence-IV Full Scale Intelligence Quotient (Full Scale-IQ). Cerebral neurophysiological inhibition, assessed soon after birth, confirmed phosphatidylcholine's fetal developmental effects.
Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements compared to placebo produced fewer children with multiple or pervasive Withdrawn problems and increased WPPSI-IV Full-Scale IQ (mean difference 7.78, 95% CI 1.88, 13.7; p = .010). Attention problems did not decrease significantly. In exploratory analyses, 11 children had CBCL1.5-5yr Autism Spectrum T-scores in the clinical referral range and language deficits typical of Autism Spectrum Disorder, 10 of 71 from women who had placebo and 1 of 71 who had phosphatidylcholine, Risk Ratio 10.0; 95% CI 1.31, 76.1; p = .026. Twelve children had Full-Scale IQ > 120 (>90 %ile), 10 of 54 from women who had phosphatidylcholine and 2 of 49 who had placebo, Risk Ratio 4.54; 95% CI 1.05, 19.7; p = .044. Positive effects were observed regardless of presence or absence of maternal mental disorders. Phosphatidylcholine produced no significant adverse effects or safety problems for women or children. Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and hypertension were not increased. The children had normal physical parameters at birth and through childhood. Several limitations temper the study's findings: effects on Attention problems did not reach significance, parents rated social behavior, and one-third of women were lost between prenatal enrollment and 4-year assessments.
Prenatal phosphatidylcholine supplements provide safe, effective support of fetal brain development. Comparison of doses from this and previous trials suggests 6300 mg phosphatidylcholine or 900 mg choline, beginning as early as possible in gestation. Outcomes for the children include fewer social withdrawal problems and increased cognitive test performance.

title: Protein disulphide isomerase protects against ALS/FTD phenotypes associated with cyclin F in zebrafish and cellular models.
abstract:
Mutations in CCNF, encoding cyclin F, cause a small proportion of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) cases. Mutant cyclin F mislocalises from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, impairs the ubiquitin proteasome system, disrupts endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to Golgi transport, and triggers ER stress and apoptosis. Protein disulphide isomerase (PDI), a redox-active ER chaperone of the thioredoxin superfamily, protects against ALS phenotypes induced by mutant SOD1, TDP-43, and FUS, but its activity against mutant cyclin F has not been examined.
To test whether PDI overexpression prevents the cellular and behavioural phenotypes induced by the ALS/FTD-associated cyclin FS621G mutation.
Neuro-2a cells were co-transfected with mCherry-tagged wild-type or mutant cyclin FS621G and V5-tagged PDI or empty vector. Subcellular localisation, XBP-1 and CHOP activation, proteasome reporter (GFPu) accumulation, nuclear morphology, and cleaved caspase-3 immunoreactivity were assessed by confocal microscopy. Transient transgenic zebrafish larvae generated by mRNA co-injection of cyclin F and PDI were assessed by photomotor response at 48 h post-fertilisation.
Mutant cyclin FS621G induced cytoplasmic mislocalisation, ER stress (assessed by XBP-1 and CHOP activation), proteasome dysfunction (indicated by GFPu accumulation), and apoptosis (assessed by nuclear condensation and caspase-3 activation), all of which were significantly attenuated by PDI co-expression. Zebrafish larvae expressing cyclin FS621G swam significantly shorter distances than uninjected or wildtype controls, and co-expression of PDI restored motor function to near-wildtype levels.
PDI protects against ALS/FTD-associated mutant cyclin F in both cellular and in vivo zebrafish models, identifying PDI as a redox-based therapeutic target for CCNF-linked ALS/FTD.

title: Therapeutic potential of varenicline in neuropsychiatric disorders: insights into its molecular mechanisms.
abstract: Neuropsychiatric disorders pose significant health challenges. Current drug therapies are often inadequate, highlighting the urgent need for new and effective treatments. The α4β2 nicotinic receptor has been implicated in the pathophysiology of various neuropsychiatric disorders. In this context, varenicline, its selective agonist, has garnered increasing attention for its potential therapeutic effects across a range of neuropsychiatric conditions. Emerging preclinical evidence suggests that varenicline may exert neuroprotective effects through modulation of pathways that include synaptic plasticity and synaptic proteins, neuroinflammation, microglial activation, apoptosis, and autophagy. However, direct target engagement for many of these pathways has not yet been established. In this review, we provide a comprehensive review of the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which varenicline might be expected to exert therapeutic effects in a range of neuropsychiatric disorders. Most previous reviews of varenicline have concentrated on its use as a smoking cessation aid or on its potential to treat individual diseases. The current review takes a different approach, focusing at the molecular level on the various pathways that are affected in different diseases, and discussing within each section the evidence that currently exists in relation to each of these in studies conducted in rodent models and in clinical trials. The review seeks to provide insight into the potential benefits and drawbacks of using a single compound to treat a variety of disorders, and to highlight areas for future research.

title: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome in an Elderly Woman on a Haloperidol-Lithium Combination: A Diagnostic Challenge with Complete Recovery.
abstract: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is a rare but potentially fatal idiosyncratic reaction to dopamine-blocking agents, characterized by hyperthermia, generalized rigidity, autonomic instability, and altered consciousness. Its recognition is particularly difficult in elderly patients, in whom the presentation may be atypical and the differential diagnosis broad. We report a 76-year-old woman with chronic schizophrenia, maintained on haloperidol and lithium for approximately 3 months, who presented with high-grade fever (39.6°C), acute alteration in sensorium, and hypertension (170/110 mmHg). Examination revealed lead-pipe rigidity, bilateral tremor, and a Glasgow Coma Scale of 10/15. An initial working diagnosis of infectious encephalitis produced a diagnostic delay of 2-3 days; lumbar puncture and blood cultures were unremarkable, and creatine kinase peaked at 4120 U/L. NMS was diagnosed using diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders, fifth edition (DSM-5) and Levenson criteria. Both offending agents were withdrawn, and the patient was managed in intensive care with intravenous hydration, active cooling, bromocriptine, and lorazepam. She achieved complete neurological recovery by day 14 and was discharged without residual deficits. This case underscores that NMS must be considered early in any older patient on dopamine antagonists presenting with fever, rigidity, and altered consciousness and that the haloperidol-lithium combination carries a specific risk even at therapeutic lithium levels.

title: Integrating dispersive liquid-liquid microextraction with HPLC-MS/MS for simultaneously determining urinary tobacco exposure biomarkers and neurodevelopmental metabolites.
abstract: Tobacco smoke exposure (TSE) during early life is a major public health concern, as the thousands of toxic and neurotoxic compounds present in cigarette smoke can critically disrupt brain development. Dysregulation of neurotransmitter levels has been linked to oxidative damage and an increased risk of neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders. Despite its clinical relevance, simultaneous quantification of neurotransmitters and tobacco metabolites in urine remains challenging due to their broad polarity range and the complexity of the biological matrix. To address this gap, we developed a novel hydrophilic interaction ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry (HILIC-MS/MS) method for the simultaneous quantification of 21 urinary biomarkers, including three tobacco-specific biomarkers, sixteen neurotransmitters and related metabolites, and two oxidative stress biomarkers. Sample preparation combines a clean-up step prior to the metabolite extraction by dispersive liquid-liquid microextraction from only 1 mL of urine, effectively reducing matrix effects to below 10% without enzymatic hydrolysis or derivatisation. The method achieved limits of detection as low as 0.004 ng/mL for NNAL, with extraction recoveries of 83-92% for tobacco biomarkers, 69-111% for neurotransmitters, and 83-94% for oxidative stress biomarkers. Repeatability and reproducibility were below 5% for all compounds, confirming the robustness of the method. The method was successfully applied to urine samples from children living with smoking adults, revealing possible neurotransmitters and oxidative stress alterations linked to the exposure. These findings demonstrate the suitability of the proposed approach as a reliable, sensitive, and high-throughput analytical tool for large-scale biomonitoring studies investigating the early biochemical effects of tobacco smoke exposure on neurodevelopmental health outcomes.

title: Ferroptosis in health and disease.
abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent, non-apoptotic form of regulated cell death that is driven by lipid peroxidation. In the past decade, it has emerged as a core pathogenic mechanism in a wide range of human diseases, such as neurodegenerative disorders, cardiovascular disease, cancer, and notably, reproductive dysfunction. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular mechanisms underlying ferroptosis with a specific focus on the System Xc⁻-GSH-GPX4 axis, iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, and the regulatory roles of key modulators such as Nrf2, ACSL4, and CISD2. This review also explores the physiological roles of ferroptosis in development, tissue homeostasis, and immune regulation, as well as its pathological contributions to obesity, diabetes mellitus, atherosclerosis, neurodegeneration, stroke, cancer, infectious diseases, and reproductive disorders. A substantial part of this review discusses the role of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of reproductive disorders, such as male reproductive pathologies, including varicocele, testicular ischemia-reperfusion, cryptorchidism, oligospermia, erectile dysfunction, and testicular cancer, and female pathologies like primary ovarian insufficiency, polycystic ovary syndrome, endometriosis, ovarian cancer, and pre-eclampsia. Moreover, the interplay between ferroptosis and immune dysfunction in reproductive tract infections was highlighted. Furthermore, we evaluated current biomarkers, emerging therapeutic strategies, and key translational challenges, highlighting the promise of ferroptosis-modulating agents for novel diagnostic and therapeutic interventions in reproductive medicine and beyond.

title: Is psychomotor retardation a sixth domain of negative symptoms?
abstract:
The five canonical domains of negative symptoms in schizophrenia - blunted affect, alogia, asociality, anhedonia, and avolition - were established by a consensus process. Meta-analyses have placed psychomotor retardation (PMR) rating scale items in negative symptom factors, suggesting it may be a sixth negative symptom domain.
We pooled data from two cross-sectional, multicenter, international studies of schizophrenia (N = 271) and used PANSS item G7 (Motor Retardation) as a measure of PMR. In multivariate analyses we examined G7 as a predictor of cognitive function, personal and social function, and negative symptoms other than PMR. We also examined whether G7 mediated the association between extrapyramidal symptoms and negative symptoms.
In some analyses the G7 factor had relationships characteristic of the five canonical domains: correlations with those negative symptoms and negative correlations with function and cognition. However, other findings were consistent with its classification as a motor symptom: significant correlations with the PANSS Mannerism and Posturing item and with extrapyramidal symptoms, and mediation of the relationship between extrapyramidal symptoms and the canonical negative symptoms. There was no significant relationship with self-reported hours of sleep.
PMR showed associations with negative symptoms, cognitive impairment, and functional outcome, consistent with status as a sixth negative symptom domain. However, other findings leave unclear whether it should be considered a negative symptom, a motor symptom, or something more complex. Problems in the G7 item definition and description contribute to this uncertainty.

title: Constructing functional neural circuits to model amyotrophic lateral sclerosis with induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoids.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the degeneration of both upper and lower motor neurons. Recent advances in human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoids offer an innovative platform to model amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in a human-specific context. These three-dimensional organoid systems allow for the study of neuronal circuit-level dysfunction, which is central to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis pathogenesis, by incorporating multiple neuronal subtypes and supporting glial populations. In particular, the integration of region-specific brain organoids into assembloid models has enabled the reconstruction of functional long-range projections and cortico-motor circuits, closely resembling human neural connectivity. This review summarizes the generation and application of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoids for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis research, with a focus on the reconstruction of neural circuits, multi-omics profiling, and functional assays. We also discuss how organoid systems can be leveraged for drug discovery and personalized medicine in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, highlighting their potential to unveil human-specific disease mechanisms. Lastly, we address the current challenges and future directions for improving the physiological relevance of organoid models in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis research.

title: A Machine Learning-Guided Lyric Analysis Peer Support Intervention (LAPSI) for Psychological Distress in South African Women: Protocol for an Exploratory Sequential Mixed Methods Study.
abstract:
Psychological distress disproportionately affects women in South Africa and is shaped by complex structural, socioeconomic, and psychosocial determinants, particularly within the context of HIV. Despite policy commitments to integrate mental health services into existing health systems, current interventions are limited in their capacity to address these intersecting determinants and are frequently insufficiently targeted, contextually responsive, or inclusive. Data-driven strategies that identify subgroup-specific vulnerabilities may improve the design of contextually relevant and culturally grounded psychosocial interventions.
This study seeks to develop and implement a machine learning (ML)-informed lyric analysis peer support intervention (LAPSI) and to evaluate its preliminary impact, feasibility, and acceptability among South African women living with or at heightened risk of HIV.
An exploratory sequential mixed methods design is used across five phases: (1) a scoping review of mental health interventions in sub-Saharan Africa; (2) ML-based risk profiling using national survey data with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP)-based interpretability; (3) intervention development and implementation; (4) a single-arm pre-post quantitative assessment of psychological distress using the Kessler 10-Item Psychological Distress Scale (K10), without a comparison group; and (5) qualitative evaluation of feasibility, usability, and acceptability.
Secondary data analyses were conducted between October 2024 and April 2025. LAPSI was implemented between May and August 2025 in 2 provinces. Outcome assessments were completed in August 2025 (Eastern Cape) and September 2025 (Gauteng), and qualitative interviews were conducted 5 to 7 days after the intervention. A total of 30 participants were recruited and completed the intervention. Quantitative and qualitative analyses were ongoing at the time of manuscript submission, with full findings anticipated to be reported in 2026 and 2027.
This protocol describes a potentially scalable framework for integrating explainable ML with culturally grounded, peer-delivered intervention design to address psychological distress among women in HIV-affected settings.

title: Glymphatic dysfunction in early-onset schizophrenia: DTI-ALPS index reduction tracks illness burden and is independently associated with cognitive performance in treatment-resistant patients.
abstract: Early-onset schizophrenia (EOS) is associated with greater cognitive impairment than adult-onset disease, and many patients also develop treatment resistance. Glymphatic dysfunction has been described in adult schizophrenia but not in EOS or in relation to treatment resistance. We used diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) to assess glymphatic function in 30 adolescents with EOS (15 treatment-resistant, TRS; 15 non-treatment-resistant, nTRS) and 29 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HC). Participants completed a neuropsychological battery covering verbal memory, processing speed, executive function, working memory, verbal fluency, and social cognition. ALPS differed across groups (F(2,56) = 34.66, p < 0.001, η² = 0.553), with values decreasing from HC (1.625 ± 0.072) to nTRS (1.501 ± 0.098) to TRS (1.439 ± 0.048); the TRS-nTRS difference was not significant (d = 0.81, p = 0.066). Patients showed broad cognitive deficits relative to HC, but nTRS and TRS did not differ on any measure after FDR correction. ALPS showed a nominal inverse association with the number of psychotic episodes (ρ = -0.391, p = 0.033) but was unrelated to PANSS scores or antipsychotic dose. Within TRS, ALPS was independently associated with phonemic verbal fluency (COWAT: β = +0.74, p = 0.003); a parallel association with categorical fluency (β = +0.88, p < 0.001) was partly driven by an influential observation and is exploratory. Glymphatic dysfunction appears to be a disease-intrinsic feature of EOS, lowest in TRS, possibly linked to cumulative episodes rather than current symptoms, and may contribute to cognitive impairment in treatment-resistant patients.

title: A shape deformation-based framework for constructing individualized subcortical morphological networks.
abstract: Individualized morphological brain networks have emerged as an important framework for imaging-based connectomics. However, existing methods have focused predominantly on the cerebral cortex, leaving subcortical structures largely unexplored despite their central roles in cognition and neuropsychiatric disorders. Here, we developed a novel framework for constructing individualized subcortical morphological networks from structural magnetic resonance imaging. Specifically, subcortical surfaces were reconstructed using a Point2Mesh-optimized multilayer perceptron architecture and vertex-wise shape deformation was quantified as the signed Euclidean distance between each vertex on an individual mesh and the corresponding vertex on the group-average template mesh. Interregional morphological connectivity in local shape deformation distributions was subsequently estimated using Jensen-Shannon Divergence. Applying this approach to the Human Connectome Project dataset, we found that subcortical morphological networks exhibited complex topological organization, including small-world architecture, modular organization, and highly connected hubs, which were consistently preserved at finer subregional scales. Analyses using an independent test-retest dataset further demonstrated fair-to-good reliability of these network properties. Importantly, these shape deformation-based networks showed significant coupling with subcortical functional networks estimated from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Leveraging large-scale multisite clinical datasets, we further demonstrated alterations of subcortical morphological networks in schizophrenia and major depressive disorder. Schizophrenia was characterized predominantly by right caudate-centered disruptions in morphological connectivity and nodal centrality, whereas major depressive disorder exhibited alterations only in nodal centrality of the right amygdala. Together, these findings establish a novel and reliable framework for investigating subcortical morphological network organization in the human brain across both healthy and psychiatric populations.
